title: An Abstract
identity: David Ward’s An Abstract is an alto saxophone and piano work published by Southern Music, copyright 1963. Hal Leonard identifies publisher level 3; WorldCat confirms score format and original publication. Fred Hemke recorded it; Paul Brodie also included it in a solo collection with practice recording. The Philharmonie guide and a 2005 UNT faculty-list survey use different historical pedagogical categories.

evidence.claim: Publisher page identifies David Ward, alto sax, Southern Music SS101, eight pages, Level 3.
WorldCat lists the score as alto saxophone and piano, published 1963.
UNT dissertation table of recorded examples identifies Fred Hemke’s recording.
Brodie advanced solo collection listing includes this work and a Paul Brodie alto performance with piano accompaniment.
The guide calls the work atonal and places it in its fifth-year framework.
evidence.source_name: Claude Delangle et al., 10 ans avec le saxophone (Philharmonie de Paris digital scan)

evidence.claim: The 2005 UNT dissertation’s appendix reports that An Abstract appeared on one selected college/university repertoire list, labeled freshman by that list. This is a historical survey result, not a current placement recommendation.
evidence.source_name: Scott D. Kallestad, University of North Texas DMA dissertation (2005)

review_focus: No score inspected. Publisher level and advanced-solos compilation are conflicting difficulty signals; inspect the edition before interpreting.
collection_flag: Original alto saxophone and piano work. Historical pedagogical sources place it in contrasting systems: fifth-year French guide and one U.S. college list’s freshman label.

listening.description: Paul Brodie, alto saxophone with Antonin Kubalek, piano; listed on Music Minus One collection.

gaps: No score pages inspected and no audio auditioned.
The publisher Level 3 and Music Minus One compilation context differ; neither should be translated directly into Tim’s study-year scale.
